title: Becanus’s close: three ways mortal and venial are not alike against the law—FINIS Prior
source_text: XXXI. Unde colligit peccatum veniale & peccatum mortale non esse eodem modo contra legem. Primo, quia mortale est ita contra legem, ut sit etiam contra finem legis; non item veniale. Secundo, quia omne mortale est perfecte contra legem; multa venialia imperfecte. Tertio, quia omnia mortalia sunt contra legem aliquam, quae simpliciter necessaria est ad salutem; venialia deliberata non item.
pass_a_gloss: Whence he gathers that venial sin and mortal sin are not against the law in the same way. First, because mortal is so against the law that it is also against the end of the law; not likewise venial. Second, because every mortal is perfectly against the law; many venials imperfectly. Third, because all mortals are against some law which is simply necessary unto salvation; deliberate venials not likewise.
pass_b_english: Becanus closes Prior: mortal alone wars also with the law’s end, and always perfectly, against precepts needful to salvation.
Deliberate venials lack that triple sameness—so the Roman map of mortal vs venial ends here before the Protestant Pars Posterior.
